ACT, PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION TO RS.7,79,400/- (EXCLUDING THE AMOUNT AWARDED BY THE TRIBUNAL) ALONG WITH INTEREST BY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD OF THE I ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT KALABURAGI DATED 01.10.2019 IN MVC NO.726/2017.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the claimant in MVC.No.726/2017 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, at Kalaburagi (hereinafter for short referred to as 'Tribunal') against judgment and award passed in the said case dated 01.10.2019, claiming for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. The matter is posted for admission and with consent of both side advocates', case is taken up for final disposal.
The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.

04. The brief facts of the case are that on 13.07.2016 the claimant met with an accident in Basavakalyan due to rash and negligent driving of Tata Indica Car bearing Reg.No.KA-25-Z-5927 by its driver.
As a result of which, the claimant had sustained grievous head injuries, injuries to the chest, face, internal injuries to the back, right leg and other parts of the body.
He took treatment in Government Hospital, at Basavakalyan and for higher treatment at Upase Surgical and Maternity Hospital, Omerga Dist: Maharastra State.

entities.text: Upase Surgical and Maternity Hospital, Omerga Dist: Maharastra State
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He had taken treatment as inpatient from 13.07.2016 to 06.08.2016.
He has been suffering from permanent disability.
05. It is further case of the claimant that he is an agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he has been suffering from permanent disability, which is Pundalik S/O Nagappadevbal vs Siddalingeshwar S/O Sangayya Nargal ... on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150695693/
2 affecting his earning capacity.

sentences.text: With these reasons he prayed to award compensation of Rs.11,45,000/-.
The insurer denied all the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
07. From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for its determination.
08. The claimant to prove his case, examined PW.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.

The respondent No.2 had not led oral evidence, however, got marked Ex.R.1.
09.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record, by the impugned judgment awarded the following amount of compensation :-
Sl. Heads of Compensation Amount No.
01.

Injury pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
02.

Medical expenses Rs.1,46,300/-
03. Food and extra nourishment and Rs.10,000/-
 medical attendant 04. Conveyance Rs.08,000/-
05. Loss of income during treatment Rs.22,500/-
06.

Permanent disability Rs.1,18,300/-
07. Deprivation of future amenities Rs.20,000/-

Total compensation Rs.3,65,600/-
 NC: 2024:KHC-K:3722 10.
Heard the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - insurance company.
11. The learned counsel for the claimant has contended that the disability taken by the Tribunal is on lower side.
The income of the claimant assessed by the Tribunal is also on lower side.
The amount of compensation awarded on all the heads are on lower side and hence, prayed for enhancement of the compensation.

12. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - insurer would submits that the Tribunal had awarded just and reasonable compensation and there are no reason for interference and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

3 13.
There is no serious dispute regarding the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, age of the claimant and other particulars in this appeal.
Insurer had not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
14. The Tribunal had taken the income of the claimant at Rs.7,500/- per month.
Admittedly, there are no materials on record to prove the income of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3722 claimant.

Therefore,
the notional income is taken as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
Income of the claimant is taken at Rs.8,750/- per month.
The multiplier applicable in the present case is 11 and disability is 12% as assessed by the Tribunal.
The same is accepted.
On the basis of the same, the compensation is re
- calculated towards loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability.
15. The amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads except medical expenses are on lower side and it needs to be enhanced.

Accordingly, the following amount of compensation is awarded :-
Sl
. Heads of Compensation Amount No.

01. Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
02.

Medical Expenses Rs.1,46,300/-
03.

Misc. Expenses such as special Rs.30,000/-
 diet, conveyance charges,
 attendance charges 04. Loss of income during the Rs.52,500/-
 treatment (Rs.8,750/- x 6)
05. Loss of future income due to Rs.1,38,600/-
 permanent disability  (Rs.8,750/- x 12 x 11 x 12%)
06.
Loss of amenities Rs.40,000/-
The claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.91,800/-.

The claimant is also entitled for interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation amount from the date of petition till its realization.
17.
It is not in dispute that the respondents No.1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 - insurer is liable to pay the said amount.

entities.text: ORDER Pundalik S/O Nagappadevbal vs Siddalingeshwar S/O Sangayya Nargal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, at Kalaburagi in MVC.No.726/2017 dated 01.10.2019 is modified.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iii. The claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,57,400/- as against Rs.3,65,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation of Rs.91,800/- with NC:
2024:KHC-K:3722 interest on the enhanced amount of compensation at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
iv.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company shall deposit the said amount with interest within a period of 02 months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v. The amount enhanced is meager.
Therefore, the Tribunal is directed to release the entire amount in favour of the claimant, on due identification.
The registry is directed to send back the Trial Court records to the concerned Court, with copy of this judgment.
